blocking_findings: Wider scope than described (reledmac.xslt ~4029-4039, diff lines 94-101). The old run-in separator was `$within and not($crosses) and not(@f:parallel-block = 'true') and matches(following non-empty sibling, '^[\p{L}\p{N}\p{Ps}]')`. Its replacement, the second disjunct, is `$within and matches(...)`. The `not($crosses)` and `not(@f:parallel-block = 'true')` guards are gone. The change was described as adding only the parent::j:conditional disjunct and removing the following-sibling stamping case, so this is an extra change in behaviour. It is unexplained and untested. The note-suffix `\ ` now also goes after crossing notes and after originals marked parallel-block, when the next text starts with a letter, digit or opening bracket. If either kind is emitted as a block or out of the text flow (for example the `\instructionnote{\pstart…}` form accepted in test_keep_together_geometry), a `\ ` in vertical mode starts a new paragraph that opens with an indent and a space. Fix: put the guards back inside the second disjunct only: `($within and not($crosses) and not(@f:parallel-block = 'true') and matches(...))`. Or, if dropping them was intentional, add one TeX-level test each for a crossing note and a parallel-block note showing no stray `\ ` after the closing brace.
nonblocking_findings: Previous blocker (double word space) is closed. All the separator cases are now OR-ed into one xsl:if, so each note gets at most one `\ `. That covers an in-tree rubric before a conditional, a rubric nested in j:conditional, and the f:needs-space-after copy.

Third disjunct, nested-in-conditional case: this is right for the actual source shape `<j:conditional><tei:note type="instruction">R</tei:note>text…</j:conditional>`. The note is emitted before the bracket, so the separator belongs after the note's closing brace, not after the bracket.

Third disjunct edge case: `not(matches(string(.), '\s$'))` checks the note's own trailing text, not whitespace in the source after the note. (a) If note-content normalises or trims its text, a note ending in a space gets no `\ ` and the rubric touches the bracket again. (b) In `<j:conditional><tei:note>R</tei:note> inside…`, the separator is emitted before the bracket and the source space also lands inside it, giving `R [ inside`. That depends on whether \OSCondBeginInline or the scope trims a leading space. Neither case is in the regression; one fixture with a leading space inside the conditional would cover both.
